title: ITR-4 (Sugam) for AY 2026-27: Eligibility, Presumptive Taxation & Filing Guide
description: ITR-4 (Sugam) is a simplified income tax return form for resident individuals, HUFs, and partnership firms (excluding LLPs) opting for presumptive taxation. I.

faq.a: ITR-4 (Sugam) is for resident individuals, HUFs, and partnership firms (excluding LLPs) with a total income up to ₹50 lakhs, who opt for presumptive taxation under Sections 44AD, 44ADA, or 44AE.

Presumptive taxation is a simplified scheme that allows eligible small taxpayers to declare their income at a prescribed rate (e.g., 6%, 8%, or 50% of turnover/receipts) instead of maintaining detailed books of accounts and undergoing audits.

faq.q: What are the turnover limits for presumptive taxation under Section 44AD and 44ADA for AY 2026-27?
faq.a: For Section 44AD, the limit is ₹3 crore if cash receipts are ≤5% of total receipts, otherwise ₹2 crore. For Section 44ADA, the limit is ₹75 lakhs if cash receipts are ≤5% of total receipts, otherwise ₹50 lakhs.

faq.q: Can I claim expenses if I opt for presumptive taxation?
faq.a: Under presumptive taxation, a fixed percentage of turnover/receipts is deemed as profit, and no further deduction for business expenses is generally allowed. The deemed income is considered after all expenses.

faq.q: What if my actual income is lower than the presumptive income?
faq.a: If you declare income lower than the presumptive rates and your total income exceeds the basic exemption limit, you will be required to maintain books of accounts and get them audited.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to continue presumptive taxation once opted for?
faq.a: Under Section 44AD, once you opt for presumptive taxation, you must continue it for the next five years. If you opt out before this period, you become ineligible for the scheme for the subsequent five assessment years.

faq.q: What is the due date for filing ITR-4 for AY 2026-27?
faq.a: For non-audit cases, the due date for filing ITR-4 (Sugam) for AY 2026-27 is August 31, 2026.
